visual.title: The constant C slides the wave sideways
visual.caption: For y = sin(x − C), a positive C moves the wave to the right by C. With C = π/2 the sine wave starts a quarter turn later, so its value at x = π/2 is 0 instead of 1.

predict.question: How does y = sin(x − π/2) move the graph of y = sin x?
predict.explain: The inside expression is zero when x = π/2, so the cycle starts there. A subtraction inside the function shifts the graph to the right by π/2.
